elementaryTheoremLedger.claim: A synchronous radius-R local rule on fixed adjacency has an exact radius-RT causal cone after T steps.
elementaryTheoremLedger.falsifier: Two matched initial states agreeing on the radius-RT neighborhood produce different root states within T updates without an adjacency rewrite or differing broadcast.
limitations: not valid across undeclared structural rewrites
requires a fixed combinatorial bound for metric-defined neighborhoods
elementaryTheoremLedger.method: Induct on the number of synchronous updates and the nested neighborhoods each update can read.
elementaryTheoremLedger.scope: Deterministic synchronous L0 rules on a fixed declared adjacency, with identical broadcasts when L1 data are present.

elementaryTheoremLedger.claim: Neighborhood-isomorphism local kernels with equivariant synchronous commit commute with every carrier relabeling.
elementaryTheoremLedger.falsifier: A carrier permutation changes an intrinsic output while all neighborhood data and conflict resolution are transported equivariantly.
elementaryTheoremLedger.method: Transport every rooted decorated neighborhood and corresponding write through the carrier isomorphism.
elementaryTheoremLedger.scope: Finite decorated carriers and rules that exclude absolute IDs and serialization order from their read semantics.

elementaryTheoremLedger.claim: State-only updates on a fixed finite carrier preserve its homology and Euler characteristic.
elementaryTheoremLedger.falsifier: A combinatorial invariant changes while every cell and boundary matrix remains byte-identical.
limitations: scale-dependent inferred topology may change even when exact carrier topology does not
elementaryTheoremLedger.method: The chain groups and boundary matrices are identical at every time, so their ranks, kernels, images, and alternating cell count are identical.
elementaryTheoremLedger.scope: Any trajectory whose cell sets and boundary operators remain unchanged.
tests: topology remains constant under release-1 diffusion and curvature steps

elementaryTheoremLedger.claim: No deterministic equivariant radius-R observer running for T rounds distinguishes roots with isomorphic radius-RT decorated neighborhoods and matched broadcasts.
elementaryTheoremLedger.falsifier: A bounded observer returns different root histories for two coupled radius-RT-identical inputs.
limitations: does not restrict observers with growing radius or trusted global data
elementaryTheoremLedger.method: Couple the two executions through the rooted isomorphism and apply the causal-cone and equivariance propositions.
elementaryTheoremLedger.scope: Bounded-round deterministic distributed recognition on declared rooted decorated carriers.

assumptions: valid links for the surface conclusion
elementaryTheoremLedger.claim: Positive shared edge lengths satisfying strict triangle inequalities define a piecewise-Euclidean triangular length space; valid vertex links make it a surface with boundary.
elementaryTheoremLedger.falsifier: A face satisfying all strict inequalities lacks a Euclidean SSS realization, or equal shared edges cannot be glued isometrically.
limitations: intrinsic construction does not prove an embedding in three-space
elementaryTheoremLedger.method: Apply side-side-side realization facewise, glue equal edge copies isometrically, and use the path/cycle link criterion.
elementaryTheoremLedger.scope: Finite triangular complexes with one authoritative length per abstract edge.

elementaryTheoremLedger.claim: Positive tangency-circle radii with edge lengths l_ij=r_i+r_j satisfy every strict triangular face inequality.
elementaryTheoremLedger.falsifier: Positive radii yield a nonpositive triangle slack under l_ij=r_i+r_j.
limitations: does not establish prescribed-curvature realizability
elementaryTheoremLedger.method: Each triangle slack reduces exactly to twice the radius at the intervening vertex.
elementaryTheoremLedger.scope: Triangular faces in the positive tangency circle-packing metric.

elementaryTheoremLedger.claim: Angle defects on a finite nondegenerate triangulated surface, using interior target angle 2pi and boundary target angle pi, sum to 2pi times Euler characteristic.
elementaryTheoremLedger.falsifier: An exact valid triangulation violates the symbolic angle-count identity under the stated boundary convention.
limitations: floating residuals are computational audits
the total condition is not sufficient for a target metric
elementaryTheoremLedger.method: Sum face angles, use 3F=2E_i+E_b and E_b=V_b, then identify the Euler alternating count.
elementaryTheoremLedger.scope: Compact finite triangular two-manifolds with boundary and nondegenerate Euclidean faces.
tests: release-1 disk, sphere, puncture, and invalid-surface fixtures

elementaryTheoremLedger.claim: The zero-eigenvalue multiplicity of the symmetric normalized Laplacian equals the number of connected components.
elementaryTheoremLedger.falsifier: An eligible graph has normalized-Laplacian nullity different from its component count.
elementaryTheoremLedger.method: Characterize the kernel from the nonnegative Dirichlet quadratic form component by component.
elementaryTheoremLedger.scope: Finite undirected graphs with positive edge weights and the declared zero-block isolated-vertex convention.
tests: release-1 connected and disconnected spectral fixtures

assumptions: same edge flux used at both endpoints
elementaryTheoremLedger.claim: A symmetric edge-flux update conserves the declared measure-weighted total exactly in algebra.
elementaryTheoremLedger.falsifier: The symbolic weighted sum changes under a finite symmetric flux update.
limitations: conservation alone does not ensure positivity or time-step stability
elementaryTheoremLedger.method: Pair and cancel the two oriented contributions of every undirected edge.
elementaryTheoremLedger.scope: Finite graphs with symmetric nonnegative conductance and the stated antisymmetric neighbor-difference update.

elementaryTheoremLedger.claim: When circle-radius edge-sum equations are solvable on a connected graph, radii are unique exactly when the graph is nonbipartite; a bipartite graph retains a one-dimensional alternating gauge.
elementaryTheoremLedger.falsifier: A solvable connected nonbipartite instance has two radius solutions, or a connected bipartite instance has a homogeneous solution outside the alternating line.
limitations: positivity bounds restrict but do not generally remove the bipartite gauge
elementaryTheoremLedger.method: Differences of two solutions alternate sign along paths; an odd cycle forces the root difference to zero.
elementaryTheoremLedger.scope: Connected finite graphs and real solutions of r_i+r_j=l_ij on every edge.

elementaryTheoremLedger.claim: Changing every edge length of a fixed connected N-vertex graph by at most epsilon changes every shortest-path distance by at most (N-1)epsilon.
elementaryTheoremLedger.falsifier: A pairwise distance changes by more than (N-1) times the maximum edge perturbation.
limitations: a useful refinement bound additionally requires the rescaled factor to vanish
elementaryTheoremLedger.method: Evaluate each old shortest simple path in the perturbed metric and reverse the argument.
elementaryTheoremLedger.scope: Fixed finite connected graphs with positive edge lengths.

elementaryTheoremLedger.claim: A closed deterministic generator, seed, parameter record, broadcast sequence, and synchronous update determine one finite trajectory.
elementaryTheoremLedger.falsifier: Two executions with the identical closed record produce different exact finite states before environment-only metadata.
limitations: floating libraries may require schema-aware tolerance rather than byte equality
elementaryTheoremLedger.method: The initial state is fixed by the closed record; induction fixes each subsequent deterministic update.
elementaryTheoremLedger.scope: Finite computations without undeclared nondeterministic inputs.
tests: Global Geometry II checksum and manifest fixtures

elementaryTheoremLedger.claim: Straight inherited subdivision of a piecewise-Euclidean complex is isometric to the original piecewise-Euclidean realization.
elementaryTheoremLedger.falsifier: A path changes intrinsic piecewise-Euclidean length under a purely inherited straight subdivision.
limitations: a changed graph one-skeleton distance is not the same metric
elementaryTheoremLedger.method: The identity on every old face preserves every rectifiable path length before and after partition.
elementaryTheoremLedger.scope: Facewise straight subdivisions with consistent shared-edge subdivisions and inherited Euclidean lengths.

assumptions: declared square and triangular generator sets
elementaryTheoremLedger.claim: Unit-edge square and triangular one-skeleton refinements have different normed-plane metric limits: the square unit ball has four extreme points and the triangular unit ball has six.
elementaryTheoremLedger.falsifier: An integer coordinate contradicting either word-distance formula, or a surjective normed-space isometry preserving neither extreme-point count, would refute the stated proof fixture.
limitations: does not obstruct a shared covariance-normalized diffusion limit
does not apply when both meshes are given a common facewise piecewise-Euclidean metric
elementaryTheoremLedger.method: Use the exact word-distance formula |m|+|n| for square generators and max(|m|,|n|,|m+n|) for triangular generators, then count the extreme points of their polyhedral unit balls.
elementaryTheoremLedger.scope: Infinite square and triangular coordinate graphs with their word metrics, rescaled by lattice spacing on bounded pointed sets.

elementaryTheoremLedger.claim: Uniform simple random walks on the orthogonal square and equilateral triangular step sets have the same covariance-normalized Gaussian finite-dimensional diffusion limit.
elementaryTheoremLedger.falsifier: A declared step moment differs from I/2, or a fixed finite collection of rescaled-time characteristic functions has a non-Gaussian or family-dependent limit.
limitations: does not prove path-space tightness
does not identify graph metrics
does not cover boundaries or disordered conductance
elementaryTheoremLedger.method: Prove the symbolic zero mean and covariance I/2 identities, expand each finite-support symmetric characteristic function at the origin, and apply Cramer--Wold after factoring joint characteristic functions over disjoint time increments.
elementaryTheoremLedger.scope: Independent-increment walks using exactly the declared physical step vectors; convergence of finite-dimensional distributions under n^{-1/2} spatial scaling.
tests: symbolic covariance identity with binary64 residual audit

elementaryTheoremLedger.claim: Centered iid bounded-range step laws with uniformly nondegenerate covariance converge uniformly over the declared bounded basin, after covariance whitening, to common standard-Brownian finite-dimensional laws.
elementaryTheoremLedger.falsifier: A law inside the declared bounded centered nondegenerate basin has a whitened fixed-time characteristic function that does not converge uniformly to exp(-|xi|^2/2), or the uniform Taylor remainder bound fails.
limitations: finite-dimensional laws only
does not prove path-space tightness in this package
does not cover estimated whitening
does not cover state-dependent, correlated, boundary, or degenerate increments
elementaryTheoremLedger.method: Whitening gives identity covariance and a uniform support bound M/sqrt(kappa); a third-order characteristic-function remainder is O(n^-3/2) uniformly, and independent increment blocks give uniform finite-dimensional convergence.
elementaryTheoremLedger.scope: Families of centered iid laws on R^d with support norm at most M and covariance eigenvalues in [kappa,1/kappa], for fixed finite observation times and Cramer--Wold coefficients after exact covariance whitening.

assumptions: continuous-time heat semigroup of the normalized graph Laplacian
evidence.claim: Closed-form square and triangular spectra evaluated in binary64 agree within the frozen finite spectral-dimension profile tolerances on every eligible intermediate window, and the cycle control remains within its registered one-dimensional tolerance.
evidence.falsifier: Invalidate this result if its bound result checksum does not reproduce, a finalized evidence or manifest digest fails, or recomputation changes any gate under the same protocol and runtime contract.
limitations: profile agreement is weaker than full geometry
bounded planar and disordered ensembles are required before a universality claim
finite-size thresholds are research protocol choices
evidence.method: Evaluate Fourier eigenvalue formulae in binary64, compute d_s(t)=2t·Σλe^{-tλ}/Σe^{-tλ}, mask scales by finite-size and zero-mode rules, compare matched windows, and apply the frozen target and cycle-control bounds.
evidence.scope: Binary64 evaluations of closed-form finite normalized-Laplacian spectra and the heat-trace analytic-log-derivative estimator only; this does not assert graph isometry, a common metric limit, full marked metric-measure-operator equivalence, or a continuum theorem.
tests: analytic spectra versus release-1 dense eigensolver on small lattices
